question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow gateway.peers sessions_send/sessions_spawn feature now, or first require a broader federation identity/scope contract before adding core cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: The source proves the capability is missing, but the requested fix adds core routing, config, credentials, session-state, and message-delivery behavior across gateway trust boundaries; that cannot be resolved safely by an automated bug-fix lane.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and use the linked FRD/security review to settle peer identity, scopes, delivery guarantees, and session-history semantics before merging implementation work.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow peer PR
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the gateway.peers direction and require the linked PR to fix conflicts, add upgrade/security proof, and show real multi-gateway behavior before merge.

options.title: Defer to external bridge/plugin paths
options.body: If core federation is out of scope for now, document supported MCP/plugin bridge workarounds and close only after maintainers decide not to provide a native primitive.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and use the linked FRD/security review to settle peer identity, scopes, delivery guarantees, and session-history semantics before merging implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent current-main history owns the affected session-tool and gateway-helper files, while the decision still needs broader product/security input.
